== Biography ==
'''Agnes Glasgow''' was baptised at Libberton, Lanarkshire, on 21 August 1720. The indexed entry names [[Glasgow-4168|Robert Glasgow]] and [[Wilson-127539|Katherine Wilson]] as her parents and records the residence as Gladhaimb.<ref name="FMP1" /><ref name="FMP20261022" /> Her birth is placed before the baptism; no separate birthday is supplied by the detailed transcript. Libberton is inferred from the baptism rather than independently established as her birthplace.

=== Wilson household reconciliation — 30 October 2026 ===

Agnes’s baptism on 21 August 1720 names Katherine Wilson and Robert Glasgow in Libberton, residence Gladhaimb (OPR 650/1, item 3, p.11). John’s separate baptism on 23 September 1722 names the same full parental couple in Libberton, residence Sandyburgh (p.17). The existing Katherine Wilson-127539 account represents that 1722 mother and the compatible 1713 Carnwath bride. Read together, the full parental-name match, same parish and two-year child sequence support identifying Agnes’s mother with this existing woman at '''95% subjective confidence · Confident'''. The 1720 maternal name was already corrected on 22 October; the new finding is the supported profile connection, not another baptism discovery. <ref name="WilsonHousehold20261030">Findmypast, Scotland Parish Births & Baptisms: [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4033335&tab=this Agnes Glasgow, 21 August 1720, Libberton, Gladhaimb, OPR 650/1 item3 p.11], parents Robert Glasgow and Katherine Wilson; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4033399&tab=this John Glasgow, 23 September 1722, Libberton, Sandyburgh, OPR 650/1 item3 p.17], parents Robert Glasgow and Katherin Wilson. Held provider transcripts compared 30 October 2026; originals uninspected. The companion 1720 indexes repeat one event.</ref>

The different farm residences are compatible with one family but do not prove a continuous address; a same-name couple remains possible. The three 1720 index versions represent one event.
